key_insight: V-Retrver converts multimodal retrieval into an evidence-driven agentic reasoning loop, letting the model actively verify fine-grained visual cues rather than relying on static language-centered Chain-of-Thought, which reduces speculative answers and improves reranking accuracy.
problem_solved: Current multimodal reranking methods are largely language-driven and use static visual encodings, causing hallucination and poor handling of visually ambiguous or fine-grained evidence during retrieval.
method: Agentic evidence loop: reformulate retrieval as an agentic process where an MLLM issues visual probes, inspects the image (or visual tokens/regions), and iteratively verifies candidate evidence.
Dynamic visual grounding: combine on-demand visual extraction (e.g., region crops, attention/heatmaps) with multimodal reasoning to produce grounded justifications for reranking.
Evidence-driven rerank: score and reorder retrieval candidates based on explicit, verifiable visual evidence and chainable reasoning steps instead of static text-only CoT outputs.
impact: Provides more accurate, robust, and explainable multimodal retrieval by reducing speculative reasoning and enabling fine-grained visual verification — useful for retrieval systems, VQA, and downstream vision-language tasks.
